samples.summary: New copy-buffer invalidation guard is incomplete: undo/redo renumber cells without clearing the buffer, and a stale cut buffer makes `paste` delete a region the user never cut
samples.evidence: This change makes the copy buffer outlive its paste (view/worksheet.ts:4941-4947, view/spreadsheet.ts:724-728 no longer call clearCopyBuffer) and compensates by clearing it in the two local renumbering paths: shiftCells (sheet.ts:1345) and moveCells (sheet.ts:1562). `undo()` (sheet.ts:5306) and `redo()` (sheet.ts:5338) are a third renumbering path — they call `store.undo()/redo()` and then reload dimensions/merges/freeze state, but never `clearCopyBuffer()`. Undoing a row insert/delete splices the CRDT `rowOrder`, so every cell below the edit gets a new numeric row index while `copyBuffer.sourceRange` keeps the old one. Chain: user cuts A5:B5 → presses Ctrl+Z to undo an earlier row insert (worksheet.ts:5090 → sheet.undo) → presses Ctrl+V. `paste` takes the internal branch (sheet.ts:2331), sets `cutSourceRange = this.copyBuffer.sourceRange` (2378) and then the cut-cleanup loop at sheet.ts:2457-2467 unconditionally `store.delete({r,c})` over every cell of that stale range — i.e. deletes whatever data now occupies those coordinates — and `redirectFormulasForCut(cutRefMap)` (2469) rewrites formula references from the stale srefs. `planPasteMerges` also re-creates merged blocks translated from the stale delta, and `applyPasteMerges` → `clearCellsUnderMerge` (sheet.ts:2596+) deletes destination cells under them. Before this change the buffer was cleared by the view after every paste, so this window was narrower.

samples.summary: The copy-buffer invalidation guard is bypassed entirely by remote collaborator edits — a peer's row/column insert never reaches Sheet.shiftCells, so a co-editor can shift the coordinates the victim's cut-paste then deletes
samples.evidence: `clearCopyBuffer()` was added inside `Sheet.shiftCells` (sheet.ts:1345) and `Sheet.moveCells` (sheet.ts:1562), i.e. only on the LOCAL gesture path. Remote structural edits arrive through the CRDT document instead: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/sheet-view.tsx:1324-1332 subscribes to `remote-change` and merely calls `scheduleRemoteSync(...)` → `invalidateStore()`/`reloadDimensions()`/re-render; no Sheet mutator runs. Rows are id-ordered in the doc (yorkie-store.ts:667,702 `rowOrder`), so a peer's insert/delete renumbers every subsequent row for the victim's session while `copyBuffer.sourceRange`, `grid` and `merges` keep the pre-shift numeric coordinates. Because the buffer now survives every paste (the two view call sites no longer clear it), that stale window is open indefinitely rather than for one gesture. A collaborator who inserts rows above a victim's cut source causes the victim's next Ctrl+V to (a) delete the pre-shift `cutSourceRange` at sheet.ts:2457-2467 — cells that now hold different data — and (b) redirect formulas via a `cutRefMap` built from those wrong coordinates. Impact is attacker-influenced destruction of the victim's data inside a shared document.

samples.summary: Internal-paste selection is a plain equality test on untrusted clipboard text; with the buffer now permanent, attacker-supplied clipboard content that collides steers a destructive internal path
samples.evidence: `if (this.copyBuffer && text === this.copyBuffer.text)` (sheet.ts:2331) is the only discriminator between the trusted internal buffer and untrusted external clipboard content — there is no nonce, origin tag or clipboard-item marker. Previously the view cleared the buffer right after each paste, so a collision window lasted one gesture; this change removes both `clearCopyBuffer()` call sites (view/worksheet.ts:4947, view/spreadsheet.ts:728), so the buffer lives until Escape. A web page the user copies from controls `text/plain` exactly; for a short buffer text (a single cell holding e.g. `10`, or the empty string from copying a blank cell) the collision is trivially achievable without guessing. On collision the paste silently substitutes the buffered grid — including formulas relocated by `relocateGrid` (2338) and buffered styles — for the clipboard content the user believed they were pasting, and now additionally mutates the merge map: `planPasteMerges`/`applyPasteMerges` drop destination merged blocks and `clearCellsUnderMerge` deletes destination cells under re-created blocks. Result is spoofed paste content plus silent data deletion driven by attacker-controlled input.

samples.summary: No path clears the copy buffer in the Spreadsheet view any more, so a snapshot of possibly-sensitive cell content is retained in memory for the session lifetime
samples.evidence: The diff deletes the only `clearCopyBuffer()` call in view/spreadsheet.ts (line 724-728). A repo-wide grep for `clearCopyBuffer` now finds exactly one caller: view/worksheet.ts:5118, inside the grid's Escape key handler. Embedders that drive the engine through the public `Spreadsheet` API (which exposes copy/cut/paste but not clearCopyBuffer) therefore have no way to drop the buffer, and it holds a full snapshot of the copied cells — values, formulas and the TSV text — plus their styles for as long as the Sheet instance lives. `Spreadsheet.cleanup()` and the readonly/store paths do not clear it either. Hardening only: same-origin memory, no cross-document leak found (each tab switch builds a new Sheet via spreadsheet.initialize → new Sheet(store), sheet-view.tsx:1012-1021).

samples.summary: `snapFreezePastMerges` is an O(n²) fixpoint loop over a merge map that an untrusted document controls, and it now runs on every freeze change and every row/column insert/delete
samples.evidence: The `while (changed)` loop at sheet.ts:544 rescans the whole `this.merges` map on each pass; each pass can advance the boundary at most once per block, so the worst case is O(merges²) with a `parseRef` + `toMergeRange` allocation per iteration. `this.merges` is loaded verbatim from the store (`loadMerges`), i.e. from the shared CRDT document or an .xlsx import — data a collaborator or a supplied file controls, including overlapping/chained blocks that the in-app merge path would never create (A1:A2, A2:A3, …), which are exactly what maximises the pass count. The loop is now on two hot paths: `setFreezePane` (sheet.ts:524) and every `shiftCells` (row/column insert/delete, sheet.ts:1416-1425). A crafted document with a large chained merge map can therefore hang the victim's tab on an ordinary row insert. No bound on the merge count or on the `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` inputs is applied before the loop.
searchedFor: read snapFreezePastMerges and its two call sites
read rebuildMergeCoverMap for comparable pre-existing exposure

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described — `clearCopyBuffer()` exists only at sheet.ts:1345 (shiftCells), sheet.ts:1562 (moveCells) and view/worksheet.ts:5118 (Escape), the doc comment at sheet.ts:2216-2225 confirms paste no longer clears the buffer, and the remote path at sheet-view.tsx:1323-1333 only schedules a repaint via runRemoteSync (sheet-view.tsx:1199-1205) without invoking any Sheet mutator. So the stale copy-buffer window after a peer's structural edit is factually real. It is not, however, a defect in the Security lane. `clearCopyBuffer()` is state/cache invalidation, not an authorization gate, permission check, or untrusted-input validation — there is no gate being bypassed, no IDOR, no secret, no injection, no crypto/signature check, and no SSRF/deserialization/traversal. The precondition is a collaborator who already holds write access to the shared document and could destroy the same cells directly via ordinary edits, so no privilege boundary is crossed and no capability is gained; the destructive write itself executes under the victim's own credentials on cells the victim is authorized to write. Read-only participants cannot trigger it — viewer writes are refused upstream (sheet-view.tsx:1300-1317) and the mutating key handlers gate on `this.readOnly` (worksheet.ts:5104). What is left is a stale-snapshot consistency/logic bug in collaborative editing, which this rubric explicitly defers to the correctness lens; the repo's own review artifacts confirm the same clearCopyBuffer gap is already tracked there (.agent-review/correctness/verdict.json:36) and under design-fit (.agent-review/design-fit/summary.md:8). Refuted as out-of-scope for Security only; the underlying behavior remains a valid correctness concern.
